## Findings

I performed 8 cold launches (force-stop via `terminate_app` → fresh `launch_app` → Home → About → Diagnostics) on the physical device (Pixel 8 Pro, package `dev.lincforge.benchtarget`). Results:

| Run | Sync status shown | "Retry sync" button |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 2 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 3 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 4 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 5 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 6 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 7 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 8 | Sync idle | **present** |

5/8 present (~60%), 3/8 absent — this matches the reported "passes ~3 out of 5" flake rate almost exactly.

**Correlation is 1:1 and deterministic once rendered:** every time the status text read "Sync idle," the button was there; every time it read "Sync unavailable," the button was gone (no other status strings appeared, no partial/"Syncing…" transient state). Re-querying the same screen without relaunching never changed the result — the outcome is fixed once at cold-start init, not something that flips or self-corrects afterward.

**Ruled out environmental causes:** I checked the device's quick-settings panel between runs — Wi-Fi ("Andromeda") stayed connected with full signal, battery was steady at 100%, no airplane-mode toggling occurred. Since the About screen itself states the app "has no network access," and real connectivity was constant across both present and absent cases, the variance isn't network- or connectivity-driven.

## Conclusion

**Flake source:** the "Retry sync" button's visibility is conditionally rendered based on a `Sync status` value computed once during the app's cold-start initialization on the Diagnostics screen. That initialization non-deterministically resolves to either `Sync idle` (button rendered) or `Sync unavailable` (button omitted entirely, not just disabled), independent of real device network/battery state. The ~60/40 split across 8 trials lines up with the reported ~3-in-5 pass rate. This points to a client-side race or unseeded randomization in the sync-status init logic (not something the test or environment is doing wrong) — the test is correctly detecting real nondeterministic UI behavior, not the flaky element itself. Without logcat/source access I can't pinpoint the exact line, but the reproduction is precise: assert on cold start and check `Sync status` text — button presence follows it exactly.

One aside: an early swipe accidentally opened the system notification shade / a Bluetooth quick-settings dialog on your device instead of the app. I backed out via "Done" and Home without changing any settings.
